hook: A $35 million whistleblower dispute was just pushed behind closed doors.

sections.voiceover: A $35 million whistleblower dispute was just pushed behind closed doors.
b_roll: A gavel striking a wooden block next to a $35 million document

sections.voiceover: On November 9, 2026, a Los Angeles judge sent Nicholas Rumanes to private arbitration. Rumanes worked as a Live Nation executive from 2022 until May 2025. Where will the $35 million evidence land?
b_roll: An exterior shot of the Los Angeles County Superior Court building
A timeline showing employment from 2022 to May 2025 at Live Nation
A large question mark over sealed court evidence folders

sections.voiceover: Except the judge preserved court authority over future discovery disputes.
b_roll: A judge signing an order reserving court jurisdiction over discovery

sections.voiceover: Arbitrator rules didn't stop oversight of Live Nation's $35 million whistleblower case. Los Angeles County Superior Court won't stop parties from bringing discovery disputes back.
b_roll: A legal document highlighting arbitrator discovery rules
A news headline graphic referencing the TicketNews report
A balance scale showing judicial oversight versus private arbitration

sections.voiceover: The $35 million lawsuit stays private, but discovery remains open.
b_roll: A legal folder closing with an open lock symbol next to it
